title: Let go
logline: The frame shop lets him go. The last mat. He carries his own drafting lamp home along 101.

panels.composition: The frame shop. The OWNER, older, glasses on a cord now. WOOD at the mat cutter. The HOURS card in the window has been replaced by one that says CLOSED SAT.

balloons.text: It's not you. It's Saturdays. There aren't any anymore.

image.prompt: an older woman with glasses on a cord speaking to a man at a mat cutter in a picture-framing shop, a new hours card in the window, muddy watercolor

panels.composition: The last mat. A forty-five. Clean. He's been cutting them eleven years.

image.prompt: close-up of hands guiding a mat cutter through a perfect clean corner, no words

panels.composition: The owner handing him the green swing-arm lamp from the backroom. His lamp; it was always hers.

balloons.text: Take the lamp. It's yours. It's been yours.

image.prompt: an older woman handing a green enameled swing-arm lamp to a thin man in a frame shop backroom
image.notes: She uses the real name once. The lamp: the Empty Chair's lamp. This is where it comes from.

panels.composition: Highway 101, afternoon. Wood walking the shoulder home with the swing-arm lamp over his shoulder like a shovel, its cord trailing. BARNABY carried in the other arm. Log trucks passing.

characters.pose: walking the shoulder, lamp on his shoulder, dog in the other arm

image.prompt: a thin man walking the shoulder of a coastal highway carrying a green swing-arm lamp over his shoulder like a shovel with its cord trailing and an old dog under his other arm, a log truck passing, watercolor, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; the Sundays the point now

notes: Let go. The lamp is the Empty Chair's lamp. He carries it home along 101 with the dog.
